compatibilityRisks: FR-8 assumes a default of 10 creations per 60 s. The existing suite appears to rely on the current default of 30, so the default stays 30. It is configurable through Shortener:RateLimitPerWindow, and operators can set 10.

FR-1 and FR-7 (ownerToken, X-Owner-Token header, expiresAt as an absolute timestamp) are not implemented. The existing contract uses X-Client-Id and expiresInMinutes, and changing it risks breaking existing tests and clients.
FR-9: loopback, private, link-local and IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals are blocked, but hostnames that resolve to private addresses are not checked. This is a documented residual SSRF risk.
Rate limiting is keyed on X-Client-Id, falling back to the remote IP. That header is spoofable, so the limit is not strictly per remote IP.
The in-memory store loses data on restart and is single-instance only.
alreadySatisfied: FR-8: FixedWindowRateLimiter is configurable, runs before validation so 400 and 409 count, returns 429 with Retry-After, and does not apply to redirects. Its counters are keyed per client (X-Client-Id, else remote IP).
FR-2: alias pattern 3-32 [A-Za-z0-9_-], reserved words (including api and r), 409 on a duplicate, case-sensitive ordinal keys.
FR-3: expiry is enforced on redirect (410) and capped at 365 days. The request field is expiresInMinutes.
FR-4: GET /r/{code} returns 302, 404 or 410. Clicks are enqueued only on a successful resolve. The ClickRecorder queue drops clicks when full, so exact counts are not guaranteed above queue capacity.
FR-5 and FR-6: metadata, analytics and the legacy /stats route exist, and the metadata response exposes no owner id.
FR-9: scheme allowlist, userinfo rejection, length limit, localhost and private/loopback/link-local/unspecified IP blocking, including IPv4-mapped IPv6.
note: Proposed by the developer agent. NOT applied to the repository; validated in a sandbox and exported for human review.
